notes: §1985:IX.1.3.5 GR3: "If the INVALID KEY phrase is not specified in the input-output statement, a USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure must be associated with the file connector and that procedure is executed and control is transferred according to the rules of the USE statement. The NOT INVALID KEY phrase is ignored, if specified." The requirement is now enforced at 85 by ExceptionPhraseRequirement.Require / HasApplicableUse (COBOL6826, the PB5076 fix, with PB5413's EXTEND arm), and the execution arm is the shared one: each KeyedIoEmitter statement passes invalidKeyHandled to EmitUseHook, whose __IoCheck (EmitUseMachinery) runs the USE procedure on a 2x status only when no INVALID KEY phrase is written, and EmitInvalid/EmitPhrasePair run NOT INVALID KEY on 0x only (IoStatusClass.InvalidKey / Successful). Probes at 85 (work-rs-04/c4): b) READ, WRITE, REWRITE, DELETE, START and a sequential-access WRITE with neither the phrase nor a USE, a DELETE with only NOT INVALID KEY, and a random file whose only USE is ON EXTEND are COBOL6826; d/e) USE ON I-O: DELETE of an absent key prints USE 23, skips NOT INVALID KEY, continues; READ of a present key runs NOT INVALID KEY; USE ON file with INVALID KEY present prints IK, not USE; USE ON INPUT runs for REWRITE 49, ON OUTPUT for a duplicate WRITE 22, ON EXTEND for a sequential WRITE 21; after a failed OPEN (35) the READ's 47 runs USE and not NOT INVALID KEY; a) a RECORD VARYING indexed WRITE of length 2 gives 44 and runs USE, neither phrase. The witness writes a duplicate key with only NOT INVALID KEY under a file-name USE. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming kb/Work PB5076 (landed); the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5076 and kb/Work PB5413 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-04.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-04-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985: if INVALID KEY is not specified 'a USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure must be associated with the file connector and that procedure is executed'. 2023 drops the requirement: §2023:9.1.14 GR3 runs any applicable exception processing statements (USE declaratives, §2023:9.1.12 GR2) and 'If control is returned from those statements or there are no applicable exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement', and §2023:9.1.14 GR4 'If the INVALID KEY phrase is not specified in the input-output statement and there are no applicable exception processing statements' continues the same way. Looser: a program with neither INVALID KEY nor USE is now conforming; EC-I-O-INVALID-KEY is nonfatal, so no refusal became a fatal exception. The paragraph on no invalid key condition is carried verbatim in GR4's trailing text.
